name: Epithelial Ovarian Carcinoma (FIGO Staging, Cytoreduction and PARP Inhibitors)

reference.source: Gynaecology by Ten Teachers 21st Edition / FIGO Committee on Gynecologic Oncology
clinicalPearls: High-grade serous carcinoma originates primarily from serous tubal intraepithelial carcinoma (STIC) lesions in fallopian fimbriae
Risk of Malignancy Index (RMI) combines ultrasound score, menopausal status and serum CA-125 level
Ovarian cancer staging is strictly surgical, requiring midline laparotomy and peritoneal washings
Complete cytoreductive surgery achieving zero visible residual macroscopic disease (R0) is the strongest prognostic factor
PARP inhibitors provide substantial progression-free survival benefit in homologous recombination deficient or BRCA-mutated tumors
reference.pathophysiology: High-grade serous ovarian cancer (HGSOC) accounts for over seventy percent of cases, arising predominantly from premalignant serous tubal intraepithelial carcinoma (STIC) lesions at the fimbriated ends of fallopian tubes harboring TP53 mutations. Exfoliated malignant cells seed across peritoneal surfaces following physiological peritoneal fluid circulation. Germline or somatic mutations in BRCA1 or BRCA2 impair homologous recombination DNA repair.
additionalDifferentials: Benign cystadenoma versus borderline ovarian tumor
Gastrointestinal adenocarcinoma metastatic to ovary (Krukenberg tumor)
Tuberculous peritonitis mimicking advanced ovarian cancer
additionalInvestigations: Transvaginal pelvic and abdominal ultrasound with color Doppler
Contrast-enhanced CT of chest, abdomen and pelvis for staging
Serum CA-125, HE4, and germ cell markers (AFP, beta-hCG, LDH in young women)
BRCA1/2 germline and somatic tumor homologous recombination testing
